title: Chapter 162: Xu Tong
html:
The “surprises” in Chen Ge’s stream were almost too spectacular. He checked the popularity chart. Qin Guang held first place. Chen Ge had begun at ninety-sixth and now ranked nineteenth.

Displayed prominently on the app’s home page, the chart’s top twenty normally belonged to major hosts with more than four hundred thousand followers. His meteoric rise drew countless curious viewers. How had a newcomer with fewer than fifty thousand followers entered an arena reserved for the platform’s stars?

Truthfully, Chen Ge had no answer. He was merely playing the “innocent victim,” had broken no law, and acted only in self-defense.

“My viewers clearly have good judgment. In a world corrupted by money, a host devoted to authentic content is a rare treasure.”

After inspecting the cameras on his chest and wrist, Chen Ge pocketed the phone and returned to the woman.

The young woman had lost control when he dragged in the attacker, repeatedly striking her head against the cage in an effort to escape. Afraid she would injure herself, Chen Ge padded the bars around her with thick cloth.

“What did she witness to leave her like this?”

He studied the three cages. The old man cowered with his arms over his head, hiding like an ostrich and refusing to look outside. Of the three prisoners, he had been confined longest and had probably witnessed the most.

At the sight of the one-armed man, the old man squeezed his eyes shut, clearly terrified of glimpsing something he should not.

The woman reacted most violently, battering her head against the bars as terror poured from her eyes. Those two responses made sense. The middle-aged prisoner’s behavior made Chen Ge far more cautious.

He too appeared frightened, trembling with his hands tightly clasped. His expression was flawless and would have deceived almost anyone. Chen Ge saw through it not because of extraordinary insight, but because he already possessed the Third Sick Hall’s patient records. This man was almost certainly Patient Number 5, Xu Tong.

If the culprits came from the Third Sick Hall, how had one of its patients become a victim? Once he asked that question, more inconsistencies emerged. Xu Tong looked relatively clean, his head remained unshaved, and he had kept both hands concealed beneath his clothes. Only when Chen Ge dragged in the attacker had he exposed one.

A deep bite wound marked his left hand and still bled.

“Your hand is injured?” Chen Ge walked to the last iron cage holding the hammer. When he entered the nurse’s station at the first sick hall, he had noticed the paint stain on the iron cage. Following the station, he had seen a splatter that was mixed with oil and blood on the wall outside of the nurse’s station.

At first, Chen Ge had assumed the blood belonged to the cage’s occupant. But the old man was uninjured, which meant it had come from whoever dragged him away.

Blood mixed with grease suggested a clear sequence: the old man had clung to the wall with greasy fingers, and his captor had tried to pry him loose, only to be bitten. That explained why both substances stained the same spot.

Neither the twisted-faced man nor his one-armed companion had an injured hand. Unless another person lived in the hospital, Xu Tong had to be the one who moved the old man from the first sick hall.

He was not merely a captive. He was one of the culprits.

When the group outside arrived, Xu Tong and his companions must have hurriedly transferred the old man to the second hall’s laundry room to keep him hidden.

As the iron hammer swayed before him, fear slowly filled Xu Tong’s eyes.

“I won’t hurt you. I merely want honest answers to a few questions.” Xu Tong continued pretending not to understand, too frightened to respond.

“You don’t feel like talking?” Chen Ge removed both cameras, set them aside, and blocked their lenses. Then he turned and drove the hammer into the cage, warping the bars with a single blow.

“Still nothing?” He struck again and again until the twisted bars reduced the prisoner’s space by a quarter.

“What… what do you want to know?” Xu Tong watched the hammer creep nearer, his expression crumbling. Why does this man seem even crazier than I am?

“I don’t force people to do anything against their will. I only have some simple questions.” Chen Ge surveyed the distorted cage and lowered his hammer. “What is your name?”

The man hesitated for two seconds. “Wang Haiming?”

“Wang Haiming?” Chen Ge’s heart lurched. He knows Wang Haiming?

Xu Tong had probably chosen a random name to deceive him, never expecting that Chen Ge knew its owner.

“You’re lying.”

Without allowing an explanation, Chen Ge swung again. The hammer shrieked through the air, raising every hair on the prisoner’s body. “My name is Xiong Qing! Xiong Qing!”

Chen Ge had no time for games. Blow after blow rained against the cage, shrinking its interior until the bars threatened to snap. “Didn’t you say you wouldn’t force anyone to do something against their will?” the man screamed.

Chen Ge ignored him. After several minutes, the cage was so deformed that even its key could no longer open it. Smashing through the bars completely would take time he did not have. His eyes narrowed as he seized the man’s calf. “One last time. What is your name?”

The prisoner hesitated, uncertain of his intent. Trapped in a hospital containing several deadly threats, Chen Ge could no longer afford kindness. He pulled the man’s calf forward and aimed the hammer directly at it.

A shrill cry tore through the night. Chen Ge felt no sympathy for anyone who locked living people in cages. He raised the hammer and pulled the man’s other leg within reach.

As the weapon descended, the prisoner recoiled and screamed, “Xu Tong! My name is Xu Tong!”

“See? Was that so difficult?” Chen Ge stopped. “If you’d been honest from the beginning, we could have avoided all this.”

He crouched beside the cage. “You mentioned Wang Haiming. What was your relationship? Was he once confined in the Third Sick Hall—is that how you know him?”
